intro: と, や and か all sit between nouns in a list, and English often translates the first two as "and". The difference is what the list claims. と closes the list: these items, and no others. や opens it: these are examples, and there are more. か offers a choice: one of these, not all of them.

skills.rule: Every item named and nothing else: と. Examples from a longer set: や (often with など). Only one of them, "or": か.
skills.explain:
Ask these questions in order.

1. Is it a choice? If the sense is "A or B", only one applies, use か: 鉛筆かペンで書いてください. か can also join clauses: 行くか行かないか, まだ決めていません.

2. If it is "and", is the list complete? If you name everything, use と: 机の上にペンとノートがあります (just those two). Counting or a fixed set confirms と: 父と母と私の三人.

3. If you are giving samples, use や: 机の上にペンやノートがあります (and other things). や usually pairs with など at the end: 東京や大阪などの大きい町.

Two traps. English "not A or B" is "neither": コーヒーも紅茶も飲みません, not か. And the comparison question "which, A or B?" uses と: 犬と猫とどちらが好きですか. と and や join nouns only; to list actions use たり.
patterns: A と B  "A and B (exactly these)"
A や B (など)  "A, B and so on"
A か B  "A or B (one of them)"
A と B と どちらが…  "which, A or B?"

examples.jp: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]にペン{と}ノートがあります。
examples.en: There is a pen and a notebook on the desk (and nothing else).

examples.jp: かばんの中[なか]に本[ほん]{や}財布[さいふ]が入[はい]っています。
examples.en: There are books, my wallet and other things in my bag.

examples.jp: 鉛筆[えんぴつ]{か}ボールペンで書[か]いてください。
examples.en: Please write in pencil or ballpoint pen.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]{か}明後日[あさって]、電話[でんわ]します。
examples.en: I'll call you tomorrow or the day after.

examples.jp: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]は掃除[そうじ]{や}洗濯[せんたく]をします。
examples.en: On my days off I do things like cleaning and laundry.

examples.jp: 東京[とうきょう]{や}大阪[おおさか]などの大[おお]きい町[まち]は家賃[やちん]が高[たか]いです。
examples.en: Rent is high in big cities such as Tokyo and Osaka.

contrast.note: A closed list: 月曜日と火曜日に行きます means you go on both days. It also means "with" before people: 友達と行きます.
An open list of examples. Using や with a total (三人, 全部) contradicts itself, because や implies there are more.
A choice between alternatives: 月曜日か火曜日に行きます means you go on one of the two days.

mistakes.bad: 家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{や}母[はは]{や}私[わたし]の三人[さんにん]です。
mistakes.good: 家族[かぞく]は父[ちち]{と}母[はは]{と}私[わたし]の三人[さんにん]です。
mistakes.note: Three people, all named: the list is complete, so と.

mistakes.bad: 月曜日[げつようび]{と}火曜日[かようび]に一度[いちど]来[き]てください。
mistakes.good: 月曜日[げつようび]{か}火曜日[かようび]に一度[いちど]来[き]てください。
mistakes.note: One visit on one of two days is a choice: か. と would ask for the visit on both days.

mistakes.bad: コーヒー{か}紅茶[こうちゃ]は飲[の]みません。
mistakes.good: コーヒー{も}紅茶[こうちゃ]{も}飲[の]みません。
mistakes.note: English "I don't drink coffee or tea" means neither one: AもBも with a negative verb.

skills.tip: All of them? と. Some of them, and more besides? や. One of them? か.
